title: Law of Mass Action and Equilibrium Constant
notes: **Law of mass action (Guldberg and Waage):** at a constant temperature, the rate of a reaction is proportional to the product of the active masses of the reactants raised to their stoichiometric coefficients.
**Equilibrium constant $K_c$:** for $aA + bB \rightleftharpoons cC + dD$, $K_c = \frac{[C]^c[D]^d}{[A]^a[B]^b}$. Concentrations are equilibrium concentrations in mol/L.
**Magnitude of $K_c$:** $K_c \gg 1$ means products dominate (reaction nearly complete). $K_c \ll 1$ means reactants dominate (reaction barely proceeds).
**Temperature dependence:** $K_c$ changes only with temperature. A catalyst changes the rate but not $K_c$ because it speeds up both forward and reverse reactions equally.
**Units:** $K_c$ has units depending on the change in the number of moles of gas: $\Delta n = (c+d) - (a+b)$.
